slides: Let's continue with the area ratio.

slides.say: So remember this rule. It's very, very important. Many similarity questions are about exactly this, the linear ratio and the area ratio.
The ratio doesn't need a one in it. Say the linear ratio is four to five.
at: the linear ratio is four to five

slides.say: We square both numbers. Four squared is sixteen, and five squared is twenty-five. So the areas are sixteen to twenty-five.
And we can go back. Say the areas are twenty-five to forty-nine. What's the linear ratio?
From lengths to areas we squared. So from areas back to lengths, we take the square root of both numbers. The root of twenty-five is five, and the root of forty-nine is seven.
at: the root of forty-nine is seven

slides.say: So the linear ratio is five to seven. A lot of students keep twenty-five to forty-nine for the sides too. But that's the ratio of the areas, not of the lengths.

slides: So from lengths to areas, we square. From areas back to lengths, we take the root.

slides.say: Now let's look at circles. Here's a big circle and its diameter.
Inside it, a small circle. Its diameter is exactly half of the big diameter.
So the linear ratio here is one to two. And the area ratio is one squared to two squared, one to four.
at: the linear ratio here is one to two

slides.say: So the small circle's area is exactly a quarter of the big circle's area.
Now let's add a second small circle, the same size, next to the first one. Together, their diameters fill the big diameter.

slides: This picture comes back a lot on the exam, so it's worth knowing well.

slides.say: We don't know the real areas. So let's count in ratio units. Say each small circle is one unit.
at: Say each small circle is one unit

slides.say: The big circle is four times a small one, so it's four units.
The two small circles together are two units. Four minus two is two, so two units are left outside them.
The diameter cuts the picture into two mirror halves. So the two units split equally. One unit is on top, and one unit is at the bottom.
at: one unit is at the bottom

slides.say: So the white part on top has exactly the same area as one small circle.
at: So the white part on top

slides: I call this shape the man with glasses. The two small circles are his glasses. Some people see Kenny from South Park in it, or a Batman mask.
Some questions ask which is bigger, the top part or a small circle. We don't need to calculate and subtract. We already know they're equal.

slides.say: Similar shapes have the same shape, in another size. If the size is the same too, they're congruent.
at: Similar shapes have the same shape

slides.say: The linear ratio is the ratio between matching lines. It's the same for every pair of matching lines.
at: The linear ratio is the ratio

slides.say: And the area ratio is the linear ratio, squared. To go back from areas to lengths, we take the square root.
at: the area ratio is the linear ratio, squared
